historical_claims.anchor: In their Section 1, Davis and Kahan state explicitly that no assumption is made that the projections are spectral projectors or that the spectra of the two blocks are disjoint.
This is the classical reason, central to Kato's perturbation theory, that isolated spectral subspaces move continuously.

related_resources.reason: Statement of the spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators; read the projection-valued-measure formulation.
Definition and properties of projection-valued measures used to define spectral projections for Borel sets.
Detailed notes on projection-valued measures and spectral integrals, for the infinite-dimensional construction.
Invariant subspaces; compare with the reducing condition, which coincides with invariance for self-adjoint operators.
Resolvents and the Riesz contour-integral projection onto an isolated part of the spectrum.
